rv.q: Like the legendary music catalog from Motown, the revival that re-opened Thursday night at the Nederlander Theatre is alternately catchy and soulful, and overstuffed with memorable melodies.
If you plan to see Motown: The Musical because you're a fan of R&B icons like Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross and Stevie Wonder, then you won't be disappointed.
Even with this relentless exposure, Gordy himself remains something of a mystery.
But who’s coming to see “Motown” for anything other than the fabulous songbook?
One is ultimately powerless to resist the onslaught of great songs.
If you can ignore the cringe-inducing book scenes, you will probably have a good time.
This time around, I didn’t fall.
Still, this elaborate, very busy production ought to please anyone looking to take a nostalgia trip and overlook its problems.
But Motown, the musical shines far less brightly, lacking smarts as well as soul.

"It plays as an entirely different, and noticeably less compelling, show than the original version that ran on Broadway...This is not to say I was an enormous fan of that incarnation—I wasn't—but it had a size, energy, and (relative) intensity that this one lacks...It's imparted a jagged choppiness that keeps the evening from cohering...
Among the best things I've ever seen on a stage.
You'd have to be a curmudgeon of the highest order not to enjoy this show.
The irresistible Motown catalog is the real star here.
But if the book disappoints, the dynamic company is well worth catching.
